newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro sees possible new loss on Lille-Frigg.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro sees possible new loss on Lille-Frigg.

text.p: Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA said on Monday production problems at the North Sea Lille-Frigg gas condensate field meant it may have to write down the carrying value of its investment of about 470 million crowns.
Hydro has a 33 percent stake in the Lille-Frigg field, which is operated by Elf Petroleum.
"In September 1996, the operator of the Lille-Frigg ...informed the licensees that the start up of technical modifications for two shut-in wells on the field was not successful.

"Sufficient information is not available at this time to evaluate if either of the wells can be restored. To this extent production problems are not resolved, estimated recoverable reserves and future reveunes may be significantly reduced and Hydro's carrying value of the investment of approximately NOK 470 million may not be fully recoverable," a company sataement said.
Norsk Hydro took a write-down of 755 million crowns in the second quarter 1995 due to a 40 percent reduction in recoverable reserves at the field.

"Hydro will evaluate the need for recording an impairment loss related to the Lille-Frigg field when further information regarding production forecasts for the Frigg area ia avaliable," the company said.
